title: Activities

e Internal requests or requirements — rescheduling the planned date

It is possible to change the planned disconnection date by way of the rescheduling process. For example, you might not
have any technicians who are available to visit the disconnection site on the original agreed date. In this case, you will need

to reschedule the visit and thus, need to change the planned disconnection date.

Rescheduling therefore, is defined as the modification of the planned disconnection date and is typically initiated by the
utilities provider and not by the customer.

For more information on rescheduling a planned disconnection, see Rescheduling of Disconnection and Reconnection

Orders.

Note that is is not possible to change either of the the disconnection dates (agreed date or planned date) if a service order has
already been generated.

Activities

Disconnection orders are usually generated in a workflow step. You can also generate them directly using the Change
Disconnection Document transaction (from the SAP Easy Access menu, select |)+UtilitiesIndustry > CustomerService » Process
Execution » Disconnection/Reconnection).

If you are working in an advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) environment, the system can generate the disconnection order
automatically during the dunning run. For more information, see Advanced Metering Infrastructure .

Disconnection Entry

Use

During the disconnection entry, you inform the system when and how which devices and flat-rate installations were disconnected.
Disconnection entry can also include confirmation of the corresponding disconnection order.

Integration

When entering disconnections, you can:

e Post charges

e Enter meter reading results for disconnected devices

e Change budget billing plans

Prerequisites

You can maintain parameters for the disconnection entry in Customizing for the disconnection processing variant. You can for

example define whether budget billing plan change are admissible or whether disconnection charges are to be levied.
